newsitem.title: DUBAI: Air conditioners worst Saudi power guzzlers - report.
newsitem.headline: Air conditioners worst Saudi power guzzlers - report.

text.p: Some 75 percent of the electricity used in Saudi homes goes to air conditioners, the Saudi Press Agency (SPA) said on Friday.
It quoted a King Saud University report as also saying domestic power consumption could be reduced by 30 percent if houses were properly insulated.
Hard pressed to meet rapidly rising power consumption, Saudi officials have organised campaigns telling citizens that saving electricity is a patriotic duty.
Saudi newspapers have criticised people who habitually leave on their lights and air conditioners even when they go out.
Power consumption peaks in the summer when air conditioners run full tilt 24 hours a day to battle temperatures sometimes topping 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahranheit).

Saudi Arabia said in February it planned to invest 438 billion riyals ($117 billion) on power projects in the next 25 years to raise production capacity to 70,000 megawatts from the present estimated 20,000 megawatts.
